title: SCF entity registry
description: The shape of scf-core/registry/registry.json, the normative field set referenced by spec/scf-spec.md §2.1. This document constrains the registry's STRUCTURE so a third party can consume it without running the reference implementation. It says nothing about which entities exist or what they mean — that is the registry itself and the specification respectively.

generatorVersion.description: Version of generate_registry_json.py that wrote this file. Distinct from schemaVersion: the generator can change without the field set changing.

frameworkColumns.description: Columns present on every entity table, in DDL order. Spec §2.2.

tierLabels.description: What each tier band is called, keyed by tier as a string. Descriptive only — spec §2 states that tier carries no semantics. Present so that a consumer labelling a tier does not have to invent a name; absent in registries written before schema 2.12.

uuidExtraTables.description: Non-entity tables that carry uuid row identity (spec §6.1).

ownedTables.description: SCF's own tables that carry NO row identity — a title page is a property of the screenplay rather than a row. Together with uuidExtraTables and the entity names, this is the known table set of spec §1.3; anything else is unknown content under §10.1. Absent in registries written before schema 2.10, where it reads as empty.

entityCount.description: Must equal the length of `entities`; a consumer can use it as a truncation check.

identifier.description: A SQL identifier written by SCF. Lowercase snake_case, and never starting with the reserved prefixes `x_` (third-party extensions, spec §10.3) or `scf_` (§10.2).

name.description: Table name. Also the key [[links]] and reference fields resolve against.

nameField.description: Field to render as this row's name. For most link entities this column is not a name and the field declares `hidden: true` — see spec §2.3.

tier.description: Depth band, 0-6. Descriptive only: spec §0.7 states that tier carries no semantics.

parentEntity.description: Direction-cascade parent (spec §7), not ownership. Ownership is derived from field naming — see §2.3.

subject.description: The entity this one is about. A link entity's subject is one of the rows it joins — which is why character_relationship, whose subject is `character`, is not covered by junction tooling (spec §6.5).

scope.description: The positional grain this entity is keyed at.

paired.description: True when this entity joins two others — the thirteen link entities of spec §6.3.

positionPattern.description: Which of spec §4.5's three patterns a resolver must apply. `none` for entities with no position.

refines.description: Entities this one adds detail to. Empty for most.

queries.description: Canonical queries this entity serves. Informative: the linter requires it to be non-empty, since an entity no query reaches is unreachable data.

autoInjected.description: True for framework columns the generator adds rather than the author declaring.

hidden.description: The column is not to be displayed as a name. Spec §2.3.

polymorphicType.description: Present on a POLYMORPHIC reference: names the sibling column saying which table this one points into. Such a column carries no referenceEntity, because its target is chosen per row. Spec §12.1.2 drops these from a projected row; a column whose name ends _id WITHOUT this property is an ordinary value or an ordinary reference and MUST NOT be dropped. Absent in registries written before schema 2.12.

referenceEntity.description: Target entity for a reference field. Every field whose referenceEntity is `asset` counts as a use of that asset — spec §8.6.
